claims.statement: An existing repository's default branch can be changed; the linked procedure is separate evidence. Capability is not a universal change requirement, authorized mutation or proof of protection migration.

Absent an explicit different branch, the repository default branch is the base for new pull requests and code commits. The explicit override means default selection is not mandatory targeting of every operation.

Creation of a repository with content produces a single first branch that becomes default. The content prerequisite matters; this does not establish a branch in an empty repository or mandate a particular branch name.

Default-branch naming for new repositories can be configured through referenced personal, organization and enterprise-policy routes. This differs from changing an existing repository's default; linked pages are not automatically reviewed and scope inheritance or precedence is not proven here.

Classroom assignments have a title and optional deadline, with configurable visibility and access permissions for generated repositories. Autograding and dedicated student discussion are optional capabilities, not mandated public visibility, universal grading or evidence of actual assignments.

Classroom autograding uses configured assignment tests and describes execution on each student push, with results visible to the student for iterative changes. Test execution does not itself prove correct learning assessment, sufficient test coverage, passing work, or actual native execution; no student data was accessed.
